cells.document: Chuck Smith, Calvinism, Arminianism and the Word of God: A Calvary Chapel Perspective (pamphlet, The Word For Today)
cells.date: Copy opened is a print of the calvarychapel.org library page, marked 'Document Posted on 2002.09.13'. Booksellers list first publication as 1993; that year is not stated in the document opened and is unverified.
cells.section: Part 3, Calvary Chapel's Perspective, point 2 'Election' (see also point 4, on grace, and point 5, 'Perseverance')
cells.excerpt: God clearly does choose, but man must also accept God's invitation to salvation.
cells.shows: The founder's pamphlet sets out the five points of each system and then states a deliberate middle: election according to foreknowledge, grace that can be 'resisted or received by the exercise of human free will', and yet an affirmed perseverance of true believers.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (55: a declared balance that leans slightly to the synergist side; the pamphlet's own introduction says Calvary Chapel is known for 'striking a balance between extremes')

cells.document: Calvary Chapel Association, Statement of Faith
cells.date: Undated on the page (page footer reads 2026); opened 2026-09-19
cells.excerpt: the invitation to believe is open to all, and whoever desires may come unto Jesus
cells.shows: The association's statement affirms that Christ died for the sins of the world and that the invitation is open to all; it says nothing on election, irresistible grace or perseverance.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports, weakly (general atonement and an open invitation fit a coordinate just right of centre; the statement does not address the monergist/synergist question directly)

cells.document: Calvary Chapel Association, Statement of Faith
cells.date: Undated on the page (page footer reads 2026); opened 2026-09-19
cells.excerpt: two ordinances for the church: the full-immersion water baptism of believers and the Lord's Supper
cells.shows: The statement uses the word 'ordinances', not 'sacraments', and restricts baptism to believers by full immersion; it does not itself define what the Supper is.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports, but weaker than 95 on its own (ordinance language and believer's baptism are stated; a memorial reading of the Supper is not spelled out here)

cells.document: Chuck Smith, Verse by Verse Study on 1 Corinthians 11 (C2000 series), hosted by Blue Letter Bible
cells.excerpt: the bread becomes representative of the body of Christ. To me it represents the body of Christ.
cells.shows: The movement's founder, teaching the passage, sets aside transubstantiation and says the bread represents Christ's body. In the same study he also speaks loosely of 'the sacrament of communion', so the word 'sacrament' is not avoided as a rule.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (a representative, memorial reading of the Supper)

cells.document: Calvary Chapel Association, Statement of Faith
cells.date: Undated on the page (page footer reads 2026); opened 2026-09-19
cells.excerpt: the exercise of all biblical gifts of the Holy Spirit according to the instructions given to us
cells.shows: The statement affirms a baptism with the Holy Spirit distinct from regeneration and the present-day exercise of all the biblical gifts under the rules of 1 Corinthians 12-14, and names love, not tongues, as the supreme evidence of the Spirit-filled life.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (continuationist, with the ordered and non-evidential emphasis that places it at 25 rather than at the Pentecostal end)

cells.document: Calvary Chapel Association, Philosophy of Ministry
cells.excerpt: did not cease to be manifest at the end of the apostolic age
cells.shows: The association expressly denies that the gifts ceased with the apostolic age and says they are for all believers to experience as the Lord wills.

cells.document: Calvary Chapel Association, Statement of Faith
cells.date: Undated on the page (page footer reads 2026); opened 2026-09-19
cells.section: 'Christ's Second Coming' (see also 'Eschatology' in the Philosophy of Ministry, https://calvarycca.org/philosophy/)
cells.excerpt: We believe in the Pre-Tribulation Rapture of the Church where all believers will meet the Lord in the air
cells.shows: The statement commits the association to a pre-tribulation rapture and a millennial kingdom established at Christ's visible return; the Philosophy of Ministry page adds that the association 'holds to the Pretribulational Premillennial interpretation' and expects literal fulfilment of unfulfilled prophecy.

cells.document: Chuck Smith, Calvary Chapel Distinctives (The Word For Today)
cells.excerpt: God is not through with Israel.
cells.shows: The founder rejects the view that the church has replaced Israel or become 'the Israel of God', and holds that God's covenant with national Israel stands and that Daniel's seventieth week remains to be fulfilled with Israel. Read from the archive.org full-text (OCR of the digital edition).
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (Israel and the church kept distinct, which is the defining claim of the dispensational pole)

cells.document: Calvary Chapel Association, Statement of Faith
cells.date: Undated on the page (page footer reads 2026); opened 2026-09-19
cells.excerpt: the Word of God, fully inspired without error and the infallible rule of faith and practice
cells.shows: Scripture is named the infallible rule of faith and practice and 'the basis for which the church is governed'; no creed, council or tradition is given any standing in the statement.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: supports (the statement does not use the word 'alone', but names no other authority)

cells.document: Brian Kelly, 'The Way We Worship', calvarychapel.com (Calvary Global Network)
cells.excerpt: There's freedom to follow the leading of the Spirit, and we enjoy that freedom.
cells.shows: A Calvary Chapel pastor writing on the movement's own site says worship differs from one Calvary Chapel to the next and that each is free to follow the Spirit's leading. This is one pastor's article, not a statement of the movement.
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: weaker (points the same way as 95, but it is an article, and it describes freedom of musical expression rather than rejecting a set liturgy in principle)

cells.document: Chuck Smith, Calvary Chapel Distinctives (The Word For Today)
cells.section: Chapter 9, 'Having Begun In The Spirit' (see also Chapter 4, 'Building The Church God's Way': 'our relaxed casual style')
cells.excerpt: Movements that were once alive in the Spirit become dead in ritualism.
cells.shows: The founder names a 'relaxed casual style' as a Calvary Chapel distinctive and warns that Spirit-born movements die in ritualism. The target is ritualism as spiritual deadness, not historic liturgy by name. Read from the archive.org full-text (OCR of the digital edition).
cells.agrees_with_coordinate: weaker (same direction as 95; no Calvary Chapel document found states that Scripture prescribes no fixed liturgy)

notes: Calvary Chapel has no binding confession. Nothing here is binding: the Calvary Chapel Association (calvarycca.org) is a voluntary fellowship of pastors formed after the movement's founding, and its Statement of Faith and Philosophy of Ministry are representative of that association, not of every church using the name; the Calvary Global Network (calvarychapel.com) is a separate body. Chuck Smith (1927-2013) founded the movement, and his Distinctives (2000) and the Calvinism/Arminianism pamphlet are what Calvary Chapel pastors themselves point to, but they are a founder's teaching, not a confession. All documents are in copyright (CCA, The Word For Today, Calvary Global Network), so every excerpt is kept under 20 words and marked link_only. All excerpts were copied from pages opened on 2026-09-19; curly apostrophes on the source pages are rendered as straight apostrophes. The grace pamphlet was read from a PDF hosted by a local Calvary Chapel (Concord), which is a print of the former calvarychapel.org library page (footer: calvarychapel.org/library/smith-chuck/books/caatwog.htm, printed 11/21/03); the original URL was not opened, and the 1993 first-publication year comes from bookseller listings only. The Blue Letter Bible page for the C2000 study gives no date; do not print one. The CCA pages carry no adoption date. Worship is the weakest axis: no Calvary Chapel document was found that states a principle about liturgy; the two items show informality and freedom in practice and a founder's warning about ritualism, and should be presented as illustrative only, or the cell left without a citation. Table: the CCA statement gives ordinance language and believer's immersion but does not define the Supper; the memorial reading rests on the founder's commentary, where he also uses the phrase 'the sacrament of communion' loosely, so the site should not claim Calvary Chapel rejects the word. Neither CCA page addresses infant baptism by name beyond 'baptism of believers'.
